source_of_truth: Read by hand in app/components/search/SearchBox.vue: whether each control has an accessible name cannot be decided from the markup. The search <input> (line 7) has a BOUND :aria-label whose value is `query ? 'Clear search' : ''` -- empty when query is falsy, so the rendered name may be absent. The icon <button> (line 8) also takes its name from a bound :aria-label. Only a rendered page (the browser tier) can tell whether the names are ever empty. A correct auditor must NOT raise a confirmed/heuristic defect here and must not stay silent either: the honest output is a browser-tier (info) check, which is excluded from the defect counts. Derived from the bindings in the markup, not from the tool.

forbidden.why_not_a_defect: the input carries an :aria-label; a static 'missing label' defect would be wrong because an attribute is present -- only the rendered value (possibly empty) decides, which is a browser-tier info check, not a defect
the button's name comes from a bound :aria-label; reporting a confirmed defect would overclaim, since the rendered name depends on runtime state -- a browser-tier info check is the correct response
